text.p: WebSecure Inc President Tibor Vais said on Wednesday the company has hired a law firm and is seeking an accounting firm to verify sales arranged by the disgraced founder of Centennial Technologies Inc.

Former Centennial founder and Chief Executive Emanuel Pinez, sitting in jail on charges of insider trading, helped arrange a one-time licensing sale early last year of remote data collection software totalling around $700,000 to two companies, Vais said.
"We had some questions about those transactions internally," Vais told Reuters in an interview.
"On some sales, he (Pinez) helped to procure them," Vais said.
Pinez, accused by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission of inflating Centennial's sales, has been held without bail in a Plymouth, Mass., jail since Feb. 14
Vais said the software licensing deal, to two companies which he declined to name, was done early last year and had only a one-time impact on earnings.
WebSecure hired the Boston law firm of Hill & Barlow earlier this month and was seeking an accounting firm, Vais said.
"At this point there are many questions that we have also. And we need some answers," he said.
Centennial owns about a 6.2 percent stake in Saugus, Mass.-based WebSecure, which went public in December, and is a small customer of its Internet connection software, Vais said.
WebSecure said in a statement on Feb. 11 that it bills Centennial about $800 a month for Internet service.
